facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s presented with a 1-year history of a pruritic, dark red plaque on his right upper eyelid
No remarkable medical history was noted
A 4 × 2-cm erythematous, violaceous, indurated, scaly plaque with some papules on his right upper eyelid
Routine blood tests and biochemistry analysis were within normal limits
perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates around cystically dilated follicular infundibula
Exocytosis of atypical lymphocytes into the epithelium
Admixed plasma cells, eosinophils, and multinucleate giant cells
Alcian blue staining showed focal mild follicular mucin deposition
Lymphocytic infiltrates positive for CD3, CD4, CD5, and CD7
Negative for CD8, CD20, CD30, CD79a, and CD56
CD4 to CD8 cells ratio within hair follicles > 7:1
Monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement was demonstrated
A man in his 60s presented with a 1-year history of a pruritic, dark red plaque on his right upper eyelid
No remarkable medical history was noted
A 4 × 2-cm erythematous, violaceous, indurated, scaly plaque with some papules on his right upper eyelid
Routine blood tests and biochemistry analysis were within normal limits
perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates around cystically dilated follicular infundibula
Exocytosis of atypical lymphocytes into the epithelium
Admixed plasma cells, eosinophils, and multinucleate giant cells
Alcian blue staining showed focal mild follicular mucin deposition
Lymphocytic infiltrates positive for CD3, CD4, CD5, and CD7

CD4 to CD8 cells ratio within hair follicles > 7:1
Monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement was demonstrated

concepts.why: The presence of perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates, atypical lymphocytes, and a monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement supports this diagnosis

The presence of atypical lymphocytes, a high CD4 to CD8 cell ratio, and a monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement could suggest this diagnosis, although the lack of systemic symptoms makes it less likely

The presence of a pruritic plaque, lymphocytic infiltrates, and admixed plasma cells could suggest this diagnosis, although the presence of atypical lymphocytes and a monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement makes it less likely
The presence of a pruritic plaque, erythematous skin, and follicular mucin deposition could suggest this diagnosis, although the lack of other characteristic features makes it less likely

The presence of atypical lymphocytes and a monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement, along with the lymphocytic infiltrates being positive for CD3, CD4, CD5, and CD7, and negative for CD8, CD20, CD30, CD79a, and CD56, points towards Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

rationales.F01: The patient's age and sex are consistent with Mycosis fungoides.
rationales.F03: The presence of a pruritic, dark red plaque is consistent with Mycosis fungoides and Lymphomatoid papulosis.
rationales.F05: Perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates are characteristic of Mycosis fungoides.
rationales.F06: Exocytosis of atypical lymphocytes into the epithelium is a hallmark of Mycosis fungoides.
rationales.F09: The presence of CD3, CD4, CD5, and CD7 positive lymphocytes is consistent with Mycosis fungoides.
rationales.F11: A CD4 to CD8 cells ratio within hair follicles > 7:1 is characteristic of Mycosis fungoides.
rationales.F12: Monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement is a diagnostic feature of Mycosis fungoides.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a pruritic, dark red plaque on the eyelid, perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates, and atypical lymphocytes with a high CD4 to CD8 ratio support Mycosis fungoides, with Lymphomatoid papulosis as a close runner-up due to similar histopathologic features but less specific clinical presentation.
